title: High-precision authentication of cigarettes using surface-enhanced Raman scattering spectroscopy combined with machine learning
content: Rapid and reliable authentication of genuine versus counterfeit cigarettes is challenging because products vary across brands and production batches. Here, we develop a surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS)-based screening method for cigarette authentication and evaluate it across 17 commercial brands using tobacco water extracts from genuine and confirmed counterfeit products. Method optimization identified citrate-reduced silver nanoparticles (AgC NPs) as the most reproducible SERS substrate, and an extraction temperature of 40 °C provided the best balance of signal stability and class separability. Under these conditions, eight machine-learning classifiers were benchmarked on SERS spectral fingerprints; a quadratic-kernel support vector machine (SVM) achieved the best overall performance, combining high accuracy with strong generalization while limiting overfitting. The optimized model reached 99.7% accuracy, 99.7% sensitivity, and 99.9% specificity for discriminating genuine versus counterfeit cigarettes across the 17 brands. In an external blind-sample evaluation using ten unknown cigarettes from previously uncharacterized batches, the model maintained >80.0% authentication accuracy, indicating tolerance to batch-to-batch variability. Overall, this SERS-machine learning strategy enables rapid, high-accuracy cigarette authentication and shows promise for field-deployable screening.
